summary: Idaho's Bald Mountain Lookout, rebuilt in 1960 on a site used since 1913, is now a popular Forest Service rental cabin on the Clearwater National Forest.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab with catwalk on a 41-foot timber tower

access.note: On USFS cabin rental program; reachable by high-clearance vehicle, trailers not recommended on rough sections.

visit.trail_note: Dirt road has rough spots; no water at the lookout; lock combination required.

events.note: First facility on the site: a cabin.
L-4 cab on a 50-foot pole tower.
Current R-6 flattop cab on a 41-foot timber tower.
Relief lookout Bill Berrigan recorded at the tower.
Recreation.gov states it was used as a fire lookout until 1984.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, April 24, 2009.

evidence.quote: The first facility on Bald Mountain Hill Lookout was a cabin built in 1913 which was replaced with an L-4 cab on a 50' pole tower in 1938. This R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 41' timber tower was built in 1960.

evidence.supports: Recreation.gov gives 1956 build date and 1984 end of use
evidence.quote: It was built in 1956 and was used as a fire lookout until 1984.
Refurbished in 1998, it is on the Clearwater National Forest cabin rental program.
Mr. William "Bill" Berrigan (Former Forest Fire Lookout Registry) — Relief

evidence.supports: 1980s emergency status, 2009 NHLR addition, rental program
evidence.quote:
1980s: Emergency status
2009: Added to the National Historic Lookout Register
Current: On the Rental program

evidence.supports: Access road and rental logistics, drive up, combination lock
evidence.quote: Guests can drive to the lookout in vehicles with good ground clearance, but trailers are not recommended due to some rough spots on the road.
We rented Bald Mountain in the summer of 2022. Our overall impression of it is that the exterior is very nice, the catwalk and stairs are in wonderful shape and all the windows work

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the current R-6 cab to 1960 and documents two earlier structures (1913, 1938) on the same site; Recreation.gov gives 1956 for 'built' without mentioning predecessors. Treated NHLR as more detailed and used it as primary, noting the discrepancy.

notes_for_editor: Build-year conflict between NHLR (1960, with full structure history) and Recreation.gov (1956) is unresolved; NHLR's account is more detailed so it was treated as primary. Full staffing history beyond the single 1967 relief lookout was not found within the search budget.
